title: Annotatio III §.IV: Constantinopolitanum IV (Leo Isaurus / Copronymus) — 380 Fathers ban temple images
pass_a_gloss: Hence easily were found those who would oppose themselves to the new idolomania in the Fourth Constantinopolitan Council, commonly called the Seventh Oecumenical, celebrated under Leo the Isaurian and Constantine Copronymus, by a decree of 380 Fathers unanimously made, that no images at all, least of all figures of God and of Christ, were to be tolerated in temples.
pass_b_english: Opponents of the new idolomania gathered in Constantinopolitanum IV (popularly ‘Seventh Oecumenical’) under Leo the Isaurian and Constantine Copronymus.
380 Fathers unanimously: tolerate no temple images — least of all figures of God and of Christ.
source_text: Hinc facilè inventi sunt qui novæ idolomaniæ sese opponerent in Constantinop. IV. Concilio, vulgò dicto Oecumenico septimo, sub Leone Isauro & Constant. Copronymo, celebrato, decreto Patrum 380. unanimiter facto, imagines nullas, minimè omnium Dei Christique figuras in templis tolerandas esse.

choices.why: popular name for Const. IV here
